body_markdown:
The spirit of[the 1940s Jeep Willys](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/the-appeal-of-the-willys-jeep-knows-no-borders-no-barriers/) lives on in[the Wrangler](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-2027-wrangler-jl-2a-harkens-back-to-jeeps-first-civilian-focused-model/) , which is now well into its fourth generation. Jeep has hinted that it could launch a second Willys-inspired model that would take the form of a small, electrified SUV designed for European markets.


Speaking on the sidelines of the 2026 Paris auto show, Jeep Europe boss Xavier Peugeot confirmed that the Willys-inspired model would be developed for buyers in crowded cities. This means two things. First, it will have to be small enough to fit in tight parking spaces and avoid the weight-based taxes charged by several European cities to push drivers out of SUVs. Two, it will need to be electrified to some extent to be allowed to drive into the low-emissions zones in many European countries.


Jeep stressed that the Willys-inspired model hasn’t been given the green light for production yet; It’s merely an idea at this stage. It wouldn’t go on sale until after 2030 if it’s approved, so it’s too early to provide its name, its price, and technical specifications. It’s also unclear whether the model would land as a crossover with Willys-esque styling or if it would land as a scaled-down Wrangler.


As of this writing, the smallest Jeep SUV sold in Europe is the Avenger, which is based on the same platform as the Peugeot 208, the Fiat 600, and[the Alfa Romeo Junior](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/alfa-renames-milano-crossover-to-comply-with-italian-law/) , among others. Shown below, it’s a 161-inch-long crossover available with either a turbo-three-cylinder or an electric drivetrain. It’s the best-selling Jeep in many European countries, including France, Italy, and Germany.


How much smaller can Jeep go? Good question. Building a Willys-inspired model positioned below the Avenger would put Jeep in true city-car territory, which is a segment it has never competed in. Nothing suggests that the brand’s idea is to take on the Smart car, but we could see an entry-level model that stretches between 140 and 150 inches long and has rugged, heritage-laced styling.


Jeep will also expand its European range in the opposite direction with a replacement for the Renegade that’s due out by 2030,[the Recon](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/first-look-2026-jeep-recon-offers-650-hp-and-doorless-off-roading/) that has already gone on sale in the United States, and another mid-size model that hasn’t been detailed but that’s scheduled to make its debut in 2028. Time will tell whether the Willys-inspired SUV and its bigger siblings will be sold in the United States.
